title: Ocean Beach, San Diego: a visitor's guide to the beach, Newport Avenue and Sunset Cliffs
excerpt: What to see in Ocean Beach, from Dog Beach and Newport Avenue to Sunset Cliffs, plus the pier closure, the Wednesday farmers market and the beach rules visitors miss.

seo.title: Ocean Beach San Diego Guide: Pier, Newport Ave, Cliffs
seo.description: Ocean Beach, San Diego visitor guide: Dog Beach, Newport Avenue, Sunset Cliffs, the Wednesday farmers market, the pier closure and beach rules.

heroCaption: Sunset from the rooftop deck of one of the Ocean Beach homes Cardo manages.
bodyHtml:
Ocean Beach is the San Diego beach town that never turned into a resort. It has a wide city beach, an off-leash Dog Beach, a mile and a half of sandstone cliffs, and one main street, Newport Avenue, lined with antique shops, surf shops and places to eat. This guide covers what to see, what is closed, and the local rules that catch visitors out. Details are as of November 2026.

As of November 2026

Rules and hours come from the City of San Diego and the Ocean Beach MainStreet Association, linked below. Check those pages before you go, since hours and closures change.

Is the Ocean Beach Pier open?

No. The City of San Diego lists the pier as closed to the public and planned for replacement. It has been closed since October 2023 because of storm damage and age, and the city's environmental review for a new pier was expected to reach public review in spring 2027, according to Times of San Diego. High surf on Thanksgiving 2026 caused new visible damage, per KOGO. You can still see and photograph the 1,971-foot pier from the beach and the foot of Niagara Avenue, but you cannot walk out on it.

What is the beach itself like?

The main beach runs about a mile, broken up by a few rock jetties, and has a permanent lifeguard station. City lifeguards are generally on duty from 9 a.m. to dusk. The north end has a volleyball area, and there are restrooms, showers, parking and fire pits.

The surf here is stronger than at Mission Bay or La Jolla Shores, and rip currents are common. Swim near a staffed tower, and if a current pulls you out, swim parallel to shore until you are free of it. Families with small children may prefer a calmer beach; our beach guide by kind of trip compares them. After a storm, the County advises staying out of the water for 72 hours.

What are the beach rules in Ocean Beach?

The city's beach regulations apply in full, and visitors are most often surprised by four of them:

  • No alcohol on the beach, cliffs, walkways, park areas or adjacent parking lots.
  • No glass and no smoking in the same areas.
  • Fires only in fire pits or containers, and none between midnight and 5 a.m. Burn only wood, charcoal or paper.
  • Dogs keep to set hours on the main beach: from November 1 to March 31, no dogs from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., and from April 1 to October 31, none from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. At other times they must be leashed.

Where can dogs go in Ocean Beach?

Dog Beach, at the north end where the San Diego River meets the ocean, is the city's only 24-hour beach for dogs, and dogs may run there without a leash at any hour. The rest of Ocean Beach follows the time rules above. Our guide to San Diego with a dog covers parking, other off-leash beaches and patio dining rules.

What is there to do on Newport Avenue?

Newport Avenue is the neighborhood's main street, and the San Diego Tourism Authority notes that most of OB's antique and vintage stores, bars, restaurants, artist studios and surf shops are on it. It runs straight down to the sand, so it is easy to split a day between the two. Hodad's, the burger shop at 5010 Newport, is the best known stop and often has a line at lunch.

The OB Farmers Market runs every Wednesday, rain or shine, from 4 to 8 p.m. on the 4900 block of Newport Avenue, between Cable and Bacon streets, with more than 100 vendors. The organizers ask visitors to leave pets at home.

How do you see Sunset Cliffs?

Sunset Cliffs Natural Park starts at the south end of Ocean Beach. The City describes 68 acres of bluffs, arches and sea caves, with the 18-acre cliff section running west of Sunset Cliffs Boulevard between Adair and Ladera streets. The Ladera Street area is the usual sunset spot, with street parking, small lots and no restrooms. In winter and spring, watch for gray whales on their migration.

The cliff edges are unstable sandstone. Stay on established paths and back from the edge, especially after rain, and do not climb down to the water at high tide.

What is happening in Ocean Beach this December?

The Ocean Beach MainStreet Association lists OB Holidays from November 28 to December 23, 2026, starting with Shop Small Saturday on November 28 from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus a storefront decorating contest. For events across the city, see our December 2026 holiday events guide, and keep the rainy-day list handy, since winter is San Diego's wet season.

Where to stay in Ocean Beach

Ocean Beach is mostly small houses, cottages and duplexes on narrow streets, a few blocks from the sand, and parking near the beach fills early on weekends. Cardo manages several homes in the neighborhood, including pet-friendly ones with fenced yards. You can see what is available on our booking site, or compare other coastal areas on our neighborhood guides.
